title: Chicken thigh, baked, broiled, or roasted, skin not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Skinless chicken thigh is meat from the upper leg of the bird, prepared by baking, broiling or roasting. Removing the skin reduces fat content while preserving the rich flavor and juiciness of the meat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Thigh meat contains more iron than chicken breast because of higher myoglobin levels.
During dry‑heat cooking, melted fat and Maillard reactions create aromatic compounds that enhance taste.
Chicken thighs are a staple in many cuisines: American BBQ, Indian curries, and Russian “Kurochka po‑derevenski” stews.
The edible portion is about 70 % of the raw weight; the rest is bone and connective tissue.
Proper cooking requires an internal temperature of 165 °F (74 °C) to kill harmful bacteria.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Skinless thigh provides roughly 22 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 aids amino‑acid metabolism and nervous‑system function.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc is essential for immune health and wound healing.

items.title: Lower fat than skin‑on cuts
items.content: Removing the skin cuts saturated‑fat intake, making it suitable for lower‑fat diets.

items.title: Provides selenium
items.content: Selenium acts as an antioxidant and supports thyroid function.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Undercooked chicken may harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter; cook to an internal 74 °C.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to chicken proteins.

items.title: Sodium in marinades
items.content: Marinated thighs can be high in sodium, which may be a concern for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Skinless thighs can be baked, pan‑seared, or grilled. They pair well with herbs (rosemary, thyme), spices (paprika, garlic) and marinades based on yogurt or lemon juice. Serve with vegetables, whole grains, or sliced in salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh thighs keep in the refrigerator at +2–4 °C for up to 2 days. Frozen thighs are safe for up to 9 months at ‑18 °C. Thaw frozen meat in the fridge, not at room temperature. Cooked thighs stored in an airtight container last about 3 days.
